bottom_line: In patients with type 2 diabetes without previous cardiovascular disease, atorvastatin 10 mg daily vs placebo reduced major cardiovascular events (rate reduction 37% [95% CI –52 to –17], p=0.001).
implications: In this population, atorvastatin 10 mg daily was associated with fewer first major cardiovascular events than placebo (127 vs 83; hazard ratio 0.63 [0.48–0.83]) and fewer strokes (0.52 [0.31–0.89]). Total mortality was lower numerically but not statistically significant (0.73 [0.52–1.01], p=0.059). These results support efficacy for reducing first major cardiovascular events over a median follow-up of 3.9 years, while the magnitude of any mortality effect remains uncertain based on the reported interval and p value.

major_points.text: Multicentre randomised placebo-controlled trial in the UK and Ireland.
major_points.quote: 2838 patients aged 40–75 years in 132 centres in the UK and Ireland were randomised to placebo (n=1410) or atorvastatin 10 mg daily (n=1428).

major_points.text: Participants had type 2 diabetes with no documented previous cardiovascular disease and required additional risk factors and lipid thresholds.
major_points.quote: Study entrants had no documented previous history of cardiovascular disease, an LDL-cholesterol concentration of 4·14 mmol/L or lower, a fasting triglyceride amount of 6·78 mmol/L or less

major_points.text: Primary endpoint was time to first major cardiovascular event composite (acute coronary heart disease events, coronary revascularisation, or stroke), analysed by intention to treat.
major_points.quote: The primary endpoint was time to ﬁrst occurrence of the following: acute coronary heart disease events, coronary revascularisation, or stroke. Analysis was by intention to treat.

major_points.text: Trial stopped early for efficacy per prespecified stopping rule.
major_points.quote: The trial was terminated 2 years earlier than expected because the prespeciﬁed early stopping rule for efﬁcacy had been met.

major_points.text: Primary endpoint events were fewer with atorvastatin (127 vs 83), with hazard ratio 0.63 (0.48–0.83).
Stroke was reduced with atorvastatin (hazard ratio 0.52 [0.31–0.89]).
All-cause mortality showed a non-significant reduction (hazard ratio 0.73 [0.52–1.01], p=0.059).
No excess of adverse events was noted in the atorvastatin group.
major_points.quote: No excess of adverse events was noted in the atorvastatin group.

inclusion_criteria.text: Men and women aged 40–75 years with type 2 diabetes mellitus diagnosed at least 6 months before study entry.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Men and women aged 40–75 years with type 2 diabetes mellitus (deﬁned with 1985 WHO criteria) diagnosed at least 6 months before study entry

inclusion_criteria.text: At least one of: history of hypertension, retinopathy, microalbuminuria/macroalbuminuria, or currently smoking.
inclusion_criteria.quote: considered for inclusion provided they had at least one or more of the following: a history of hypertension

inclusion_criteria.text: LDL-cholesterol concentration of 4.14 mmol/L or lower.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Mean serum LDL-cholesterol concentration during baseline visits had to be 4·14 mmol/L or lower
and serum triglycerides 6·78 mmol/L or less.

exclusion_criteria.text: Any past history of myocardial infarction, angina, coronary vascular surgery, cerebrovascular accident, or severe peripheral vascular disease (warranting surgery).
exclusion_criteria.quote: Patients were ineligible if they had any past history of myocardial infarction, angina, coronary vascular surgery, cerebrovascular accident, or severe peripheral vascular disease (deﬁned as warranting surgery).

exclusion_criteria.text: Less than 80% compliance with placebo during baseline phase.
exclusion_criteria.quote: or if during the baseline phase they had less than 80% compliance with placebo.

criticisms.text: Early termination reduced the number of observed deaths and power for mortality outcome.
criticisms.quote: The early termination of the trial meant that fewer deaths were observed than originally envisaged, reducing the power of the trial to show a signiﬁcant reduction in all-cause mortality.

criticisms.text: Power was limited for subgroup heterogeneity and within-subgroup significance due to early termination.
criticisms.quote: The power to detect small differences in treatment effect between subgroups or to detect signiﬁcance of treatment effect within subgroups is limited, particularly since the trial terminated early.

criticisms.text: Net difference in statin use between groups was about 75% rather than 100% due to noncompliance and add-in therapy.
criticisms.quote: The net difference in statin use is therefore about 75% rather than 100% if all patients had remained fully compliant with the study drug
